review_scope: Complete 57-unit Chinese–English alignment read including table, title/deck, Nitobe/Hagakure scope limits, responsibility versus ownership, ground/argument/internal-failure distinctions and final open questions. Four local corrections, no blanket retranslation.

changes.before: And Theorem Four requires the opposite direction: that a subject cannot-not be questioned, and that questioning requires the subject to be able to answer — able to say I think that standard is wrong. Shame does not supply that position: the correct response to shame is correction, not rebuttal. One thing must be acknowledged: he sees part of this problem himself, writing that giri has even degenerated into cowardly fear of censure — which is what the shame lever looks like when it runs out of control. He criticised the loss of control; he did not criticise the lever.
changes.after: And Theorem Four requires the opposite direction: that a subject must be questioned, and that questioning requires the subject to be able to answer — able to say I think that standard is wrong. Shame does not supply that position: the correct response to shame is correction, not rebuttal. One thing must be acknowledged: he sees part of this problem himself, writing that giri has even degenerated into cowardly fear of censure — which is what the shame lever looks like when it runs out of control. He criticised the loss of control; he did not criticise the lever.
changes.reason: State the requirement of questioning without an easily misread cluster of negatives; preserve the subject’s ability to answer and reject the standard.

changes.before: A more convenient line of criticism must be excluded first: that he violates the criteria he set down above — internal failure. Two common arguments for that line do not hold. The first says that judging whether a thing is worth dying for requires the dier's own judgement; the second says the tree-hollow warrior was required to endure, so why not this child. Both assume that worth dying for is settled by individual weighing. In Nitobe's system it is not. What settles it is duty — given externally by the position a person occupies. The tree-hollow warrior's duty required him to live, his task being unfinished; Genzō's substitute's duty required him to die, his position making him able to serve as a substitute. Within that system the two are consistent, not in conflict — those are not two applications of one criterion, but two conclusions of one criterion at two different positions.
changes.after: A more convenient line of criticism must be excluded first: that he violates the criteria he set down above — internal failure. Two common arguments for that line do not hold. The first says that judging whether a thing is worth dying for requires the judgement of the person who would die; the second says the tree-hollow warrior was required to endure, so why not this child. Both assume that worth dying for is settled by individual weighing. In Nitobe's system it is not. What settles it is duty — given externally by the position a person occupies. The tree-hollow warrior's duty required him to live, his task being unfinished; Genzō's substitute's duty required him to die, his position making him able to serve as a substitute. Within that system the two are consistent, not in conflict — those are not two applications of one criterion, but two conclusions of one criterion — fulfil your duty — at two different positions.
changes.reason: Restore the explicit content of the single duty criterion and repair the unnatural noun without changing the source’s argument.

changes.before: Reason two: delivering another's child to die is not the property of any one culture. Nitobe himself cites Abraham. And any system that places something — a house, a lord, a cause, a nation — above its members and declares that the interest is one and inseparable will produce the same act somewhere.
changes.after: Reason two: delivering another's child to die in someone else’s stead is not the property of any one culture. Nitobe himself cites Abraham. And any system that places something — a house, a lord, a cause, a nation — above its members and declares that the interest is one and inseparable will produce the same act somewhere.
changes.reason: Restore 替死, not merely delivering a child to death.

changes.before: The shame lever places the standard outside the subject, contrary to the direction Theorem Four requires. But SAE offers no replacement. How a community is to transmit norms to children without using shame is not answered here, and the question is not rhetorical — shame is universally used because it works. A related observation is kept: the spiritual cohesion demanded by the theorists of total war and the lever of shame treated here point in the same direction — conformity, not judgement. The difference is only of scale: shame operates within a family and a village, total war across an entire nation.
changes.after: The shame lever places the standard outside the subject, contrary to the direction Theorem Four requires. But SAE offers no replacement. How a community is to transmit norms to children without using shame is not answered here, and the question is not rhetorical — shame is widely used because it works. A related observation is kept: the spiritual cohesion demanded by the theorists of total war and the lever of shame treated here point in the same direction — obedience, not judgement. The difference is only of scale: shame operates within a family and a village, total war across an entire nation.
changes.reason: Do not turn 普遍 into an exceptionless universal; preserve 服从 as obedience in the parallel with total war.
